theme: Core Data basics: the framework, the container and the context

terms.definition: A framework from Apple that stores an app's objects and the links between them on the device.
terms.example: We use Core Data to store the user's notes.

terms.definition: An object that sets up the whole storage stack for you, so you can start saving data quickly.
terms.example: The app creates one NSPersistentContainer at launch.

terms.definition: A scratch pad where you create, change and fetch objects before you save them.
terms.example: Save the NSManagedObjectContext after you edit the note.
terms.code:
import CoreData
let ctx = NSManagedObjectContext(
    concurrencyType: .mainQueueConcurrencyType)
print(ctx.hasChanges)

video.description:
Learn to explain how an app stores objects on the device with Core Data: Core Data, NSPersistentContainer & NSManagedObjectContext, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Core Data - A framework from Apple that stores an app's objects and the links between them on the device.
NSPersistentContainer - An object that sets up the whole storage stack for you, so you can start saving data quickly.
NSManagedObjectContext - A scratch pad where you create, change and fetch objects before you save them.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: Where do the notes live?
dialogue.setting: Adding storage to a notes app

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, where should the app keep the user's notes on the device?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use Core Data. It stores our objects and the links between them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Create an NSPersistentContainer, like `c` in our code. It sets up the whole stack for you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then how do I add a note?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use `viewContext`. It is an NSManagedObjectContext, a scratch pad for your changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So Core Data saves the note when I edit it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not yet. You must save the NSManagedObjectContext first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh, I forgot to call save. That is why the note disappeared.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Edit in the context, then save. The NSPersistentContainer does the rest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Core Data is easier than I thought.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Just keep one NSPersistentContainer for the whole app.
Core Data stores our notes on the device.
